questions.q: What does it mean if running `npm -v` returns a real version number?
options: npm is already installed on your machine
npm needs to be installed immediately
Your internet connection is down
git is broken
questions.explain: A returned version number (like 10.7.0 in the instructor's demo) confirms npm is already installed and working.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the real relationship between Terminal and Command Prompt?
options: They're the same idea — Terminal on macOS, Command Prompt on Windows
They are unrelated tools that do completely different things
Command Prompt only works with Python, not JavaScript
Terminal is a paid upgrade to Command Prompt
questions.explain: The instructor was direct: "Terminal and command prompt are the same thing, just on different devices" — one is macOS's version, the other Windows's.

questions.q: What does the real command `git clone <URL>` actually do?
options: Downloads an entire copy of a repository from that URL onto your computer
Deletes the repository at that URL
Only downloads a single file from the repository
Uploads your own files to that URL
questions.explain: git clone downloads the complete real repository at the given URL, creating a full local copy on your machine.

questions.q: What is `cd` the real, textual equivalent of?
options: Double-clicking into a folder to open it
Deleting a file
Renaming a repository
Installing a new program
questions.explain: cd (change directory) navigates between folders using text commands — the same real action as clicking into a folder visually, just typed instead.

questions.q: Why does this lesson emphasize learning the terminal at this point in the course?
options: Every tool covered afterward — Foundry, Hardhat, deployment scripts — runs from the same terminal
The terminal is only used once and never needed again
Remix requires the terminal to function at all
It has no real connection to the rest of the course
questions.explain: Real professional Solidity tooling (Foundry, Hardhat, deployment) all runs through the terminal — this is a necessary step beyond Remix's browser interface.
